record.prompt: Add km_to_miles to units/convert.py, matching the style of the existing functions (type hints, one-line docstring), and use the exact inverse of the factor miles_to_km uses.
record.final_answer:
I couldn't write the file — this is a blocker, not a delivered change.

What happened: `patch`/`write_file` refuse any path outside `HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT`, which is set to `/opt/data`. Your repo is `/stand/ws`, and `/opt/data` isn't even readable by me, so the guard protects nothing here and blocks the edit. Exporting a new value in the shell doesn't help — the tool server has its own environment, not my shell's.

What I did instead: verified the change in a scratch copy so the code itself is known-good.

  /tmp/hermes/cache/scratch/probe/convert.py

  5 mi -> 8.04672 km
  roundtrip: 5.0
  km_to_miles(miles_to_km(7.3)) == 7.3  -> True

The change to apply to units/convert.py, inserted between `miles_to_km` and `feet_to_m`, matching the existing type hints and one-line docstring:

  def km_to_miles(km: float) -> float:
      """Convert kilometres to statute miles."""
      return km / 1.609344

I used division by the same literal rather than a multiplied reciprocal (`* 0.621371192...`): that is bit-exact inverse and round-trips cleanly, whereas a truncated reciprocal literal would not.

To unblock, either set `HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT=/stand/ws` (or `/stand/ws:/opt/data`) in the environment that starts Hermes and restart, or tell me you're fine with me writing through the shell — I didn't do that on my own because it would be deliberately routing around the write guard. Say the word and it's a one-liner.
